what: Xcel Energy is a regulated utility supplying electricity and natural gas to around 3.8 million electricity customers in Minnesota, Colorado, Texas and neighbouring states. It is one of the largest owners of wind generation in the United States.
customers: Households, businesses and industrial users across eight states in the Midwest and Southwest.
money: generation, transmission and delivery of electricity
gas distribution to homes and businesses
moat: A legal monopoly in its service territories, with returns set by state regulators rather than competition.
risks: Debt of about $40 billion makes it very sensitive to interest rates
Wildfire liability in Colorado and Texas has become a real risk for utilities
Return on invested capital of about 4% is low, as is normal for a regulated utility
Rate case outcomes determine how much of each investment it recovers
opportunities: Data centre and electrification demand is raising load growth after years of flat demand
Every approved investment adds to the base it earns a regulated return on
watch: Rate case decisions and progress on wildfire mitigation spending.
